newsitem.title: INDIA: Death toll at 220 in Indian dengue fever outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Death toll at 220 in Indian dengue fever outbreak.

text.p: The death toll from an unusually lethal outbreak of dengue fever in the Indian capital has risen to 220, but doctors said on Sunday the number of fatalities was steadily declining.
Dengue, a mosquito-borne disease which is also called breakbone fever, erupted in New Delhi in the last week of August during annual monsoon rains.

"Looking at the number of people dying as compared to those who are reporting sick with dengue, the figures are certainly decreasing and I think the worst is over," said Amar Singh, a doctor at the dengue control room in the capital.
At least 220 persons had died in the city and another 5,365 were admitted to hospitals with dengue, Singh told Reuters.
However non-governmental health groups say the actual figures could be much higher, adding that the official death toll does not include casualties in private hospitals.

"Data is coming from 28 hospitals only whereas the capital has more than 2,000 private nursing homes and hospitals from where no feedback on the dengue affected cases is being reported," said a doctor working with a voluntary organisation.

Accompanied by high fever, headaches and pain in muscles and joints, dengue normally runs its course in six to seven days. But a haemorrhagic form of dengue that can lead to internal bleeding and death has spread through the crowded capital.
Health officials said the outbreak had taken the largest toll of lives in 20 years.
The current outbreak, initially confined to Delhi, has now spread to the neighbouring Indian states of Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, they said.
